subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: What durable sender identity contract should OpenClaw expose for inter-session and subagent messages across protocol, transcripts, live/history events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: The fix crosses protocol schema, persistent transcript semantics, UI identity rendering, and trusted-vs-untrusted metadata boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent product/API shape alone.

options.title: Add typed sender metadata
options.body: Introduce gateway-owned per-message sender id/kind/display/avatar metadata and thread it through chat.send, sessions.send, subagent announcements, history/live events, and Control UI rendering.

options.title: Keep label-only projection
options.body: Treat senderLabel as a display hint and close the broader identity contract as out of scope, accepting weaker auditability for multi-agent workflows.

options.title: Split into narrow fixes first
options.body: Land prompt requester-name and WebChat fallback fixes while leaving durable per-message identity for a later API design.

recommendation.title: Add typed sender metadata
recommendation.body: Introduce gateway-owned per-message sender id/kind/display/avatar metadata and thread it through chat.send, sessions.send, subagent announcements, history/live events, and Control UI rendering.

likelyOwner.reason: The related provenance, sessions_send, and subagent delivery history points to steipete as the strongest routing owner for this cross-surface API decision.
